newTopics.title: How to Look at Art: See, Think, Wonder
newTopics.summary: Looking closely is a skill. Slow down, describe what you see, say what it makes you think, then ask your own questions — every artwork opens up when you do.
keyConcepts: Describe: only what you can see
Analyze: how colors, lines and shapes work together
Judge: what do you think, and why?
There can be more than one good answer
newTopics.tryIt: Look at one painting for two full minutes. Write three things you SEE, two things you THINK, and one thing you WONDER. Compare with a friend.

newTopics.title: What Is Contemporary Art?
newTopics.summary: Contemporary art is art of our own time. Artists use anything — paint, light, mirrors, video, everyday objects — and often care more about the idea than the material.
keyConcepts: Art of the present and recent past
The idea can matter most (conceptual art)
Asking questions instead of giving answers
newTopics.tryIt: Choose an everyday object. Write one sentence that turns it into an artwork — what is the idea? Give it a title and a museum label.
newTopics.imageNote: Most contemporary artworks are still protected by copyright, so this topic links to museum pages instead of showing pictures.
